task: I need a periodic backup system that I can manage from the admin panel settings. I want it to automatically send me a copy of the database at set intervals. I also need a backup restore and export section, and it needs to be very flexible and robust—a cohesive system designed correctly, in line with the code, and following best practices.

findings.title: Undefined `_render_settings` helper crashes the backup toggle
findings.detail: `cb_backup_toggle` calls `await _render_settings(cb, backup)`, but no such function is defined in the module (only `_settings_view` exists, which returns a tuple). Toggling the periodic-backup switch therefore raises NameError at runtime. There are no router-level tests, so this ships unnoticed.

findings.title: On-demand backup / `_make_archive` does not create the `backups/` directory
findings.detail: `_make_archive` writes the archive to `self._dir` (= data_dir/backups) but never creates that directory; only `start_sweeper()` does. On-demand backups (`run_now`) and upload-restore therefore fail with FileNotFoundError. Worse, create_backup only catches `SnapshotError`, so this FileNotFoundError propagates uncaught to the bot callback. Reproduced: 8 service tests fail with FileNotFoundError.

findings.title: Backup record filename is never persisted
findings.detail: `insert_backup` is called with filename='' and `update_backup_status` never sets the filename, so every record.filename stays empty. This breaks: `archive_path_for` (export and restore-by-list always return None), `delete_backup` (it unlinks `self._dir / ''` i.e. the backups/ directory, not the .zip, orphaning the archive), and `_prune_retention` (kept_names never matches any real filename, so retention deletes ALL backup-*.zip files every run).

findings.title: SQLite header validation off-by-one rejects every valid restore
findings.detail: `if header[:15] != b'SQLite format 3\x00'` compares a 15-byte slice to a 16-byte literal ('SQLite format 3' is 15 chars + NUL = 16 bytes). They can never compare equal, so `_extract_and_validate` always returns None and `restore_from_file` rejects every valid archive as 'invalid_archive', even one produced by the service itself. Verified byte lengths: literal=16, slice=15. Reproduced: test_extract_and_validate_ok fails.

findings.title: Successful restore crashes at the post-success audit after staging dir is deleted
findings.detail: On the success path, `_swap`'s `finally` runs `shutil.rmtree(db_src.parent)` (removing the `_stage/` dir containing db_src), then the success audit calls `db_src.stat().st_size` on the now-deleted file -> FileNotFoundError. Latent today (no test reaches the success audit because bugs #2/#3/#4 block it first), but it will surface once those are fixed.

findings.title: Two service tests await synchronous / non-callable objects
findings.detail: `test_create_backup_missing_db_file` does `await service._dir.mkdir(...)` (Path.mkdir is synchronous, so awaiting None raises TypeError) and `test_sweeper_creates_backup_when_due` does `await db.fetch_one` (awaits the method object -> TypeError). Both abort before asserting their intent, so the missing-DB fast-fail and the due-check behavior are never actually validated.

findings.title: No tests for the backup admin router handlers
findings.detail: All tests cover only the db/repo and service layers. The backups.py handlers (toggle, export, restore-from-list, upload-restore, delete) are entirely untested, which is exactly why the router-level defects (#1 toggle NameError; #3 restore/export/delete relying on an empty filename) shipped unnoticed.

findings.title: Router reaches into `backup._db`, bypassing the service abstraction
findings.detail: `cb_backup_open` / `cb_backup_delete_confirm` / `cb_backup_restore_prompt` call `repo.get_backup(backup._db, ...)` directly, leaking the service's private DB handle to the bot layer and violating RULES §1 (bot layer should not touch DB internals; use the service). A `BackupService.get_backup(id)` method would keep the boundary clean.
